narrative:
Good morning, Khalid Al-Rashid. Here is your FY2026 snapshot as of this morning.

**Revenue** — the Q3 forecast is USD 472.9B against the USD 492.2B budget, USD 19.3B short on price: Brent has averaged USD 72/bbl against the USD 75 deck.

**EBITDA margin** is 43.6% in the budget; each USD 1/bbl of Brent moves operating income by about USD 1.44B.

**Production** is 7.7 mmboe/d — onshore 1% below plan on the OPEC+ quota, offshore 3% below after the turnaround extension, gas 3% above as Al-Rimal phase 2 came online early.

**Cash** — free cash flow of USD 60.3B does not cover the USD 83.7B dividend; the gap is funded from cash.

**Pending your decision:** 4 items — price deck reset, gas volume uplift, trading-book hedge ratio and polymer spread reset.

signals.title: Q3 forecast $19B below the $492B budget
signals.excerpt: Lower realized prices across the chain drive the gap: crude fields −$8.3B, refining −$7.2B, gas −$1.2B and trading −$2.7B; volumes are broadly on plan.

signals.title: Brent sensitivity: $2.1B revenue per $1/bbl
signals.source: Meridian Corporate Planning — price deck model
signals.excerpt: Every $1/bbl Brent move changes FY2026 revenue by about $2.1B and net income by about $0.9B after the price-linked royalty tier and 46% effective tax.

signals.title: Dividend exceeds free cash flow
signals.excerpt: The FY2026 budget dividend of $83.7B exceeds free cash flow of $60.3B after $51.2B capex; the $23B gap is funded from cash and debt and widens to about $35B at $60 Brent.
